skill.name: backend-architect
skill.description: Expert backend architect for API design, microservices, distributed systems, resilience, observability, and operational planning.
skill.summary: Designs backend architectures with clear APIs, service boundaries, reliability patterns, and operational readiness.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Backend architecture choices can create brittle APIs and unclear service boundaries. This skill guides API contracts, service decomposition, resilience, observability, and rollout planning.
actual_capabilities: Designs REST, GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket, Server-Sent Events, and webhook API patterns.
Defines microservice boundaries, service communication, gateways, and migration strategies.
Plans retries, timeouts, circuit breakers, health checks, backpressure, and graceful degradation.
Recommends observability with logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, alerts, and runbooks.
Guides caching, asynchronous jobs, event streaming, and data integration patterns.
Reviews deployment, testing, documentation, and developer experience requirements.
limitations: It provides architectural guidance, not full production implementation.
Database schema design is deferred to a database architecture specialist.
Security guidance is pattern oriented and does not replace a formal penetration test.
Recommendations depend on accurate goals, scale targets, and operational constraints.

use_cases.title: Plan a New API Platform
use_cases.description: Define API contracts, service boundaries, reliability goals, and rollout steps before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Choose a Service Architecture
use_cases.description: Compare modular monolith, microservices, event-driven, and gateway patterns for product and team constraints.

use_cases.title: Modernize a Legacy Backend
use_cases.description: Plan strangler migrations, service decomposition, observability, and safe deployment paths for existing systems.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Backend Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new service or API.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a backend architecture for this product. Include API style, core services, data ownership, reliability needs, and rollout steps.

prompt_templates.title: Define API Contracts
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for contract-first API planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define API contracts for these user flows. Cover resources, operations, error behavior, idempotency, authentication, and versioning.

prompt_templates.title: Review Service Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this service decomposition. Identify weak boundaries, coupling risks, communication patterns, ownership concerns, and a better target architecture.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Resilience and Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production readiness plan for this backend. Include failure modes, timeouts, retries, monitoring, alerts, runbooks, and deployment strategy.

output_examples.input: Design an order management API for a marketplace with payments, fulfillment, and vendor notifications.
output: A service boundary proposal separating orders, payments, fulfillment, and notifications.
Recommended API contracts with idempotency, status transitions, and error handling.
Resilience notes for retries, dead letter queues, monitoring, and safe rollouts.

output_examples.input: Review whether our reporting backend should use synchronous APIs or event streaming.
output: A trade-off analysis covering freshness, consistency, cost, latency, and operational complexity.
A recommended event-driven design with consumer ownership and replay considerations.
Risks to validate before implementation, including schema evolution and backfill strategy.

output_examples.input: Modernize a monolith that handles users, billing, emails, and analytics.
output: A phased migration plan using clear module boundaries and strangler patterns.
Candidate services ordered by coupling, risk, and business value.
Operational requirements for tracing, deployment safety, and contract testing.

best_practices: Provide business flows, scale targets, latency targets, compliance needs, and team constraints before asking for architecture.
Ask for explicit trade-offs between simplicity, consistency, cost, operability, and delivery speed.
Request rollout, observability, failure modes, and testing plans with every major architecture recommendation.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for microservices before validating whether modular monolith boundaries are enough.
Do not skip API contracts, idempotency, authorization, and error behavior when defining endpoints.
Do not treat framework selection as architecture without discussing data ownership and operational responsibilities.

faq.question: Can this skill design APIs from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide API style, contract shape, versioning, error behavior, authentication, and documentation needs.

faq.question: Does it generate production code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on architecture, contracts, trade-offs, and implementation guidance rather than complete production code.

faq.question: Can it help with microservices?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define service boundaries, communication patterns, gateway strategy, observability, and migration plans.

faq.question: Does it cover security?
faq.answer: It covers backend security patterns such as authentication, authorization, validation, rate limits, and secret management.

faq.question: Can it compare architecture options?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare monolith, modular monolith, microservices, event-driven, and serverless approaches.

faq.question: What inputs improve the result?
faq.answer: Share user flows, data ownership, load expectations, latency needs, compliance rules, team skills, and operational constraints.
